\subsection*{Leftover Hash: Results}

\begin{definition}[Hashed seed-output distribution]
\lean{TCSlib.InformationTheory.hashPair}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p182-b005,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p207-b002
}
\statementsource{HILL99}{
  pdf-130039751e9f-p020-b009,
  pdf-130039751e9f-p021-b001
}
\label{TCSlib.InformationTheory.hashPair}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist, TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist.map, TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist.prod, TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist.uniform}
Let $S$, $\alpha$, and $\beta$ be finite sets, with $S$ and $\beta$ nonempty. Given a
function $f:S\times\alpha\to\beta$ and a probability distribution $X$ on $\alpha$,
define a distribution on $S\times\beta$ by choosing $s$ uniformly from $S$ and $a$
according to $X$, independently, and recording $(s,f(s,a))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Hashed Pair Probability]
\lean{TCSlib.InformationTheory.hashPair_apply}
\label{TCSlib.InformationTheory.hashPair_apply}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist, TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist.map_apply, TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist.prod_apply, TCSlib.InformationTheory.hashPair}
\difficulty{4}
Let $S$, $\alpha$, and $\beta$ be finite sets, with $S$ nonempty, and let $f\colon
S\to\alpha\to\beta$ and $X$ be a probability distribution on $\alpha$. For $s\in S$ and
$y\in\beta$, the distribution of $(s,f(s,x))$, with $s$ uniform on $S$ and $x$
distributed according to $X$ independently, assigns probability
$\frac{1}{|S|}\sum_{x\in\alpha:\,f(s,x)=y}X(x)$ to $(s,y)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Collision Bound for Hashed Pairs]
\lean{TCSlib.InformationTheory.collision_hashPair_le}
\statementsource{HILL99}{
  pdf-130039751e9f-p020-b009,
  pdf-130039751e9f-p022-b002
}
\label{TCSlib.InformationTheory.collision_hashPair_le}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist, TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist.collision, TCSlib.InformationTheory.IsUniversal, TCSlib.InformationTheory.hashPair, TCSlib.InformationTheory.hashPair_apply, TCSlib.InformationTheory.sum_sq_fiber}
\difficulty{5}
Let $S$, $\alpha$, and $\beta$ be finite sets, with $S$ and $\beta$ nonempty, and let
$f\colon S\to\alpha\to\beta$ be universal in the sense that for every pair of distinct
inputs in $\alpha$, at most a fraction $1/|\beta|$ of the seeds in $S$ map them to the
same output. For any probability distribution $X$ on $\alpha$, the collision probability
of the distribution of $(s,f(s,x))$, with $s$ uniform on $S$ and $x$ distributed
according to $X$ independently, is at most
$\frac{1}{|S|}\bigl(\operatorname{Coll}(X)+\frac{1}{|\beta|}\bigr)$, where
$\operatorname{Coll}(X)=\sum_{x\in\alpha}X(x)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Leftover Hash Bound]
\lean{TCSlib.InformationTheory.leftover_hash}
\statementsource{HILL99}{
  pdf-130039751e9f-p021-b005,
  pdf-130039751e9f-p022-b002
}
\label{TCSlib.InformationTheory.leftover_hash}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist, TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist.HasMinEntropy, TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist.collision, TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist.collision_le_of_hasMinEntropy, TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist.uniform, TCSlib.InformationTheory.IsUniversal, TCSlib.InformationTheory.collision_hashPair_le, TCSlib.InformationTheory.hashPair, TCSlib.InformationTheory.statDist, TCSlib.InformationTheory.statDist_uniform_le_sqrt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $S$, $\alpha$, and $\beta$ be finite sets, with $S$ and $\beta$ nonempty. Suppose
$f\colon S\to\alpha\to\beta$ is universal, and let $X$ be a probability distribution on
$\alpha$ such that $X(x)\le 2^{-k}$ for every $x\in\alpha$, for some real number $k$.
The statistical distance between the distribution of $(s,f(s,x))$, for independent
uniform $s\in S$ and $x$ distributed according to $X$, and the uniform distribution on
$S\times\beta$ is at most $\frac12\sqrt{|\beta|2^{-k}}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Affine leftover hash bound]
\lean{TCSlib.InformationTheory.leftover_hash_affine}
\label{TCSlib.InformationTheory.leftover_hash_affine}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist, TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist.HasMinEntropy, TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist.uniform, TCSlib.InformationTheory.hashPair, TCSlib.InformationTheory.isUniversal_affine, TCSlib.InformationTheory.leftover_hash, TCSlib.InformationTheory.statDist}
\difficulty{1}
Let $F$ be a finite field, let $X$ be a probability distribution on $F$, and let
$k\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $\Pr[X=x]\le 2^{-k}$ for every $x\in F$. Choose $s=(a,b)$
uniformly from $F^2$, independently of $X$, and output $(s, aX+b)$. The statistical
distance between this output distribution on $F^2\times F$ and the uniform distribution
on $F^2\times F$ is at most $\frac12\sqrt{|F|\,2^{-k}}$.
\end{theorem}
